It seems the big problem that our community had in the old country was that it both lacked direction and enforcement. Does anyone had good ideas on how to maintain high quality for both? I am thinking that we should make it very clear that this is not a general LGBT community. I think we should frequently remind submitters that this is a community for masculine gay men only. I personally am fine with this subverse staying small so long as it maintains its unique quality. However, I am just a person among many. I wanted to open this up to discussion quickly so I know if I should feel welcomed here, much like I was not in the old country for being unapologetically masculine.
+1 because I agree with you, unfortunately I have nothing else to offer on the subject :(

I also see no problem in staying small, if this is the price to maintain quality. I do wish the sub to be more active though.
I think you need to make it clear what ok to talk about, and what should be on another sub.

Admittedly nitpicking here, but I'd probably say it's more for traditionally "masculine" topics rather than specifically for masculine gay men only. I'm sure there are some more feminine guys and others who would be interested in some stuff relevant to here and we shouldn't exclude em.

In answer to your question, the sub is probably still small enough to pretty much leave it up to user discretion for now. The sidebar gives a decent description and we all came from the old country, and likely all for similar reasons so I seriously doubt any of us are SJW types.

I use the term masculine gay men because I think that is the one thing that the whole community should be centered around. The community is not just of men, but a specific type of men. I used the term to accent that fact. The reason I want to draw a hard line quickly is because of what happened in the old country. At first it was a loosening of social rules, and then the next thing that happed cakes and baking where always on the front page. I do not think this subverse should say it is accepting of more feminine guys because I do not think that we should be.

I agree with you for the most part but the issue I see with saying it's only for masculine gay men is that doesn't really address anything as far as topics. For example Ive known a more outwardly feminine guy who was into trucks and cigars while one of the most otherwise masculine guys Ive known was obsessed with Rupaul's Drag Race (which obviously wouldn't be relevant here).

It could also dissuade guys from contributing who aren't exactly lumberjacks, but at the same time aren't mincing around in a sundress, just regular guys who happen to be gay

The problem with that is there is no way for anyone to know the contributor. The feminine guy that likes masculine things will be seen as more masculine then the masculine guy that writes about feminine things. It would be an unreasonable expectation to try and keep the contributors to only 'real life' masculine men, so we have to judge people based on content. Also, there is a pretty safe amount of space between lumberjacks and bakers. I am sure most people are in the happy middle. I think we should preference those that lean more to the lumberjack then the baker.

I think I agree with everything you're saying, but not exactly the way you're saying it. I think this should be a place for unapologetically masculine gay guys to post things that interest them, but I don't want to exclude people aren't in that bucket. That's not to say that I want to water down gaybros into a clone of other gay subs, but that I take issue with saying that it's only for masc. gay men. I've met a few guys who are really into cars, but present outwardly as pretty femme guys, but some (not all) of their posts would be great contributions here. I, and the community at large, have zero ways of knowing if the poster about cars is also a drag queen. This means he is masculine at that point to me. I am advocating the exclusion of discussions that are better suited elsewhere. Pictures of your wedding or a cake you made. Their are unique problems that only masculine gay men face. I'm not sure if that really captures everything we want though.

I disagree about wedding photos ever being on topic. There are better subverses for such content. Also, almost everyone thinks they're masculine enough for something like that. A clear line is much better.

I run a small country pub that recently won the CAMRA Pub of the year in our region for the 5th time. My father has run the pub for the past 30-odd years, and over the past three years I've been slowly taking over.
I am a 21 publican who runs an award winning, 300 year old, family-run pub in Kent, England. AMA!
do you give yourself / get much time off? what do you like to do in your free time?

Yes and no in a way. I'm pretty much on call most of the time, but try to get a night away from the pub every now and then. I read a lot, and play video games (currently replaying Mass Effect 2).

Case in point just happened - I was about to reply to this, then had to spend the past three hours trying to fix the card machine.

When I do get a chance to get out I like to go to London and have a few drinks in a jazz bar (I love the Late Late Show at Ronnie Scott's), or just get out in general. I act from time to time, but lately fitting in rehearsals and work has been difficult.

I'm jealous. There's not a bar older than a century in my city. It's a shame, since drinking establishments make up so much of the culture and history of a place.

So do you find yourself reluctant to make any changes? Seems to me with a 300 year old history, even the slightest change would be difficult.

Because of the age of the building, there's a lot of changes that we physically can't make. The building doesn't have foundations, so we can't knock down walls etc. I wouldn't dream of changing the atmosphere or style of the pub however. I've kinda got a rule when it comes to changes - always add things, never take away. Things may move around, but we'll never get rid of things. Almost everything in the pub has some sort of story behind it.

Freedom of expression is an important principle to voat. Self-sufficiency is a necessary requirement of autonomy, and autonomy is necessary for freedom. To be self-sufficient voat must be profitable. My question is... How?

As of last year reddit was not profitable. This article details three ways in which reddit tries to make money.

  1. Ads. To me, this is a non-starter. reddit ads were never very profitable. The weaknesses are a large percentage of users have adblock, they are limited to unobtrusive image and text links, and, most importantly, competition. Compared to companies like Google, or Facebook, reddit lacks the customer intelligence to effectively deliver ads. Simply put, if you are an advertiser, there are much better places to go than reddit.

  2. gold. reddit gold has been a significant source of income for that site. However, the facts that reddit has a much larger user base and that gold couldn't make reddit profitable after years, mean that this may not be much of a solution. Plus, with the options to donate, it seems like voat already has this solution in hand.

  3. Merchandise at the reddit store. reddit benefits from a stronger brand and a place in the current cultural zeitgeist. Until voat has similar import, I doubt that this method could prove effective.

In general, online services become profitable when the marginal cost of one additional user is less than the marginal benefit. If it costs X to serve the site to one user, and the user has an expected value of Y, then all voat has to care about is increasing the number of users. So... how do we maximize Y?
Brainstorm: How can Voat be more profitable? Ads didn't work for reddit, gold is iffy. What's a better solution?
